blocks.h2: How We Install a Gas Line

steps.body: Routed carefully, with a shutoff at the appliance.

blocks.intro: New gas work in Geneva usually ties into existing piping, sometimes very old.

items.body: In older houses, we look for paths through the basement, closets and existing chases so walls and trim stay intact.
New lines often connect to piping that's many decades old. We check the existing pipe and valves before we add to them.
A modern range, tankless heater or generator can need more gas than the original system was built for.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Can my gas line handle a new appliance?
items.answer: Sometimes. We total the demand and upsize the line if needed.

items.preview: New gas work usually requires one.
items.answer: New gas piping usually requires a permit. We'll explain what applies.

items.q: Can you run gas in an older home without opening walls?
items.preview: Often, through the basement and existing chases.
items.answer: Often. We route through the basement and existing openings where we can and tell you if any wall work is needed.
Most residential installs are done in a day, including the pressure test.

items.q: Can you add gas logs to a fireplace that's never had gas?
items.preview: Yes, if the chimney is sound.
items.answer: Yes. We run the line to the firebox, install the valve and logs and test everything. The chimney needs to be in good shape first.

items.q: How much does gas line installation cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the run and appliance. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the run, the pipe size and the appliance. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
